# 🚀 ArzanSite Backend API - Comprehensive Documentation

## 📋 Table of Contents
- [Overview](#overview)
- [Base URLs](#base-urls)
- [Authentication](#authentication)
- [API Endpoints](#api-endpoints)
- [Error Handling](#error-handling)
- [Rate Limiting](#rate-limiting)
- [Testing](#testing)

## 🌟 Overview

The ArzanSite Backend API provides a comprehensive set of services for managing user accounts, orders, designs, payments, and more. Built with NestJS and integrated with Appwrite, it offers:

- **🔐 Secure Authentication** with Appwrite sessions (HttpOnly cookie)
- **📧 Custom Email Services** with SMTP integration
- **💳 Payment Processing** with multiple gateways
- **🗄️ Database Operations** via Appwrite
- **📁 File Storage** and management
- **⚙️ Real-time Updates** with WebSocket support

## 🌐 Base URLs

| Environment | Base URL | Description |
|-------------|----------|-------------|
| **Local Development** | `http://localhost:3000/api` | For development and testing |
| **Production** | `https://nest.arzansite.com/api` | Live production environment |

## 🔐 Authentication (Session-based)

The backend now uses a secure HttpOnly cookie for authentication instead of requiring Authorization headers.

- **Cookie name**: `appwrite_jwt`
- **How it is set**: Call `POST /api/auth/session` with a valid Appwrite JWT. The backend validates the JWT with Appwrite and sets the cookie.
- **How to call APIs**: From browsers, send requests with credentials so the cookie is included. No `Authorization` header is required.

Frontend example (browser):
```javascript
// 1) Create an Appwrite session/JWT on the frontend
// (example using Appwrite Web SDK)
import { Client, Account } from 'appwrite';

const client = new Client().setEndpoint(process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_APPWRITE_ENDPOINT).setProject(process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_APPWRITE_PROJECT_ID);
const account = new Account(client);

// If not already logged in:
await account.createEmailPasswordSession(email, password);

// Get a short-lived JWT from Appwrite
const { jwt } = await account.createJWT();

// 2) Create backend session cookie
await fetch('/api/auth/session', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  credentials: 'include',
  body: JSON.stringify({ jwt })
});

// 3) Call protected APIs with credentials (cookie is sent automatically)
const me = await fetch('/api/auth/me', { credentials: 'include' }).then(r => r.json());
```

Logout options:
- Clear backend cookie only: `POST /api/auth/oauth/logout` (clears `appwrite_jwt`)
- Invalidate Appwrite session + backend cookie: `POST /api/auth/session-logout` with `{ sessionId }`

## 📚 API Endpoints

Note: All protected endpoints accept the session cookie. In browsers, prefer cookie-based auth (no Authorization header). If you use non-browser clients, you may still send `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; the guard accepts either header or cookie.

### 🔐 Authentication (`/auth`)

#### 1. User Registration
```http
POST /api/auth/signup
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "email": "user@example.com",
  "password": "SecurePassword123!",
  "metadata": {
    "name": "John Doe",
    "first_name": "John",
    "last_name": "Doe",
    "company": "Example Corp"
  }
}
```

**Response (201):**
```json
{
  "message": "User created successfully. Please check your email to verify your account.",
  "user": {
    "id": "64f8a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0",
    "email": "user@example.com",
    "emailVerification": false,
    "$createdAt": "2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z"
  },
  "verificationEmailSent": true,
  "requiresFrontendVerification": false
}
```

#### 2. Create Backend Session Cookie
```http
POST /api/auth/session
Content-Type: application/json

{ "jwt": "<Appwrite JWT from account.createJWT()>" }
```

Sets `appwrite_jwt` HttpOnly cookie if the JWT is valid. Response:
```json
{
  "user": { "$id": "<userId>", "email": "user@example.com", "emailVerification": true },
  "message": "Session created successfully"
}
```

#### 3. Email Verification
```http
POST /api/auth/verify-email
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "token": "64f8a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0",
  "userId": "64f8a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0"
}
```

**Response (200):**
```json
{
  "message": "Email verified successfully! Welcome email sent.",
  "user": {
    "id": "64f8a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0",
    "email": "user@example.com",
    "name": "John Doe",
    "emailVerification": true
  },
  "welcomeEmailSent": true
}
```

#### 4. Password Reset
```http
POST /api/auth/password-reset
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "email": "user@example.com"
}
```

**Response (200):**
```json
{
  "message": "Password reset email sent successfully. Please check your email.",
  "emailSent": true
}
```

#### 5. Token Refresh
```http
POST /api/auth/refresh
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "refresh_token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..."
}
```

**Response (200):**
```json
{
  "access_token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...",
  "user": {
    "id": "64f8a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0",
    "email": "user@example.com"
  }
}
```

#### 6. Logout (clear backend cookie only)
```http
POST /api/auth/oauth/logout
```

Clears `appwrite_jwt` cookie.

#### 7. Get Current User
```http
GET /api/auth/me
Cookie: appwrite_jwt=...
```

**Response (200):**
```json
{
  "id": "64f8a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0",
  "message": "User profile endpoint. Implement additional profile fetching as needed."
}
```

## ❌ Error Handling

### Standard Error Response Format
```json
{
  "statusCode": 400,
  "message": "Error description",
  "error": "Error type",
  "timestamp": "2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
  "path": "/api/endpoint",
  "method": "POST"
}
```

### Common HTTP Status Codes
- **200** - Success
- **201** - Created
- **400** - Bad Request (validation errors)
- **401** - Unauthorized (invalid/missing session)
- **403** - Forbidden (insufficient permissions)
- **404** - Not Found
- **429** - Too Many Requests (rate limited)
- **500** - Internal Server Error

## 🚦 Rate Limiting

- **Default**: 100 requests per minute per IP
- **Configurable**: Via `THROTTLE_TTL` and `THROTTLE_LIMIT` environment variables
- **Headers**: Rate limit information included in response headers

## 🧪 Testing

### Swagger UI
Access interactive API documentation at:
- **Local**: `http://localhost:3000/api/docs`
- **Production**: `https://app.arzansite.com/api/docs`

### Testing Tools
- **Postman**: Import OpenAPI spec from Swagger
- **cURL**: Use examples provided above

### Authentication Testing
1. Register a new user
2. Verify email (check inbox)
3. Create Appwrite session on frontend and get JWT via `account.createJWT()`
4. Call `POST /api/auth/session` to set `appwrite_jwt` cookie
5. Call protected endpoints with `credentials: 'include'`

## 🔒 Security Features

- **Session Authentication** using Appwrite JWT stored in HttpOnly cookie
- **Role-Based Access Control** (RBAC)
- **Input Validation** with class-validator
- **CORS Protection** for cross-origin requests
- **Rate Limiting** to prevent abuse
- **Helmet.js** for security headers
- **Request Sanitization** and validation

## 📱 Frontend Integration

### Environment Configuration
```javascript
const config = {
  development: {
    apiBaseUrl: 'http://localhost:3000/api'
  },
  production: {
    apiBaseUrl: 'https://app.arzansite.com/api'
  }
};
```

### Authentication Flow (Session)
```javascript
// Create Appwrite session and backend cookie, then call APIs with credentials: 'include'
import { Client, Account } from 'appwrite';

const client = new Client().setEndpoint(process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_APPWRITE_ENDPOINT).setProject(process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_APPWRITE_PROJECT_ID);
const account = new Account(client);

await account.createEmailPasswordSession(email, password);
const { jwt } = await account.createJWT();

await fetch(`${config.apiBaseUrl}/auth/session`, {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  credentials: 'include',
  body: JSON.stringify({ jwt })
});

const me = await fetch(`${config.apiBaseUrl}/auth/me`, { credentials: 'include' }).then(r => r.json());
```

### Error Handling
```javascript
const handleApiError = (error) => {
  if (error.status === 401) {
    // Token expired, try to refresh
    refreshToken();
  } else if (error.status === 403) {
    // Insufficient permissions
    showPermissionError();
  } else {
    // Other errors
    showErrorMessage(error.message);
  }
};
```

I created a dedicated debug page and aligned the frontend with the session-cookie flow. I’ll now outline what was changed and exactly what requests the frontend is making so you can configure the backend accordingly.

### What I changed
- Added a dedicated debug page at route `/debug` containing:
  - `AuthFlowTest` (now also tests invoices/receipts and can bootstrap a cookie session)
  - `BackendConnectionTest` (now tests invoices and receipts)
  - `DebugApiTest` (adds `/auth/status`, `/invoices`, `/receipts` tests)
- Removed the debug components from other pages:
  - Removed `AuthFlowTest`, `BackendConnectionTest`, `DebugApiTest` from `Wizard` and `Index` (home). Dashboard didn’t include them.
- Unified token bridging so cookie-session and bearer-token both work:
  - Session-based tokens saved by `sessionAuthService` now sync to `tokenManager` and also to the keys the `apiClient` expects (`access_token`/`refresh_token`).
  - `tokenManager` now restores tokens from either `access_token`/`refresh_token` or `backend_access_token`/`backend_refresh_token`.
- Enabled password reset via public endpoints in the Auth hook (login/signup already worked).
- Minor scripts addition:
  - Added `"start": "vite"` and `"update": "npm update"` to `package.json`.

### Likely cause of your 401 on receipts/invoices
Your UI calls protected endpoints with `credentials: 'include'` and no Authorization header if no bearer token is present. If the backend is not setting or accepting the HttpOnly cookie properly across origins, you’ll get 401. Fix is almost always CORS/cookie options.

### Exact frontend requests (so you can configure the backend)
All of these are cross-origin, browser fetches with cookies included:
- Health/auth:
  - GET `https://nest.arzansite.com/api/health` (no auth)
  - GET `https://nest.arzansite.com/api/auth/status` with `credentials: 'include'`
  - GET `https://nest.arzansite.com/api/auth/me` with `credentials: 'include'`
- Login (email/password):
  - POST `https://nest.arzansite.com/api/auth/login`
  - Headers: `Content-Type: application/json`
  - Body: `{ "email": "<email>", "password": "<password>" }`
  - Options: `credentials: 'include'`
  - Expectation: backend sets an HttpOnly cookie for the session and may also return tokens in JSON.
- Bootstrap cookie-session (optional helper flow):
  - POST `https://nest.arzansite.com/api/auth/session-auth`
  - Headers: `Content-Type: application/json`
  - Body: `{ "sessionId": "<appwrite_session_id>", "email": "<userEmail>" }` (or `{ "jwt": "<Appwrite JWT>" }`)
  - Options: `credentials: 'include'`
  - Expectation: backend sets `appwrite_jwt` cookie.
- Token refresh (if bearer present):
  - POST `https://nest.arzansite.com/api/auth/refresh`
  - Headers: `Content-Type: application/json`
  - Body: `{ "refresh_token": "<refreshToken>" }`
  - Options: `credentials: 'include'`
- Receipts/invoices (cookie-session or bearer):
  - GET `https://nest.arzansite.com/api/receipts`
  - GET `https://nest.arzansite.com/api/invoices`
  - Headers: `Accept: application/json`
  - Options: `credentials: 'include'`
  - Expectation: either accept HttpOnly cookie or Authorization: Bearer if present.

If you want to test the exact browser pattern with curl (cookie jar mimics credentials: 'include'):

```bash
# 1) Login and capture cookies
curl -i -X POST https://nest.arzansite.com/api/auth/login \
  -H "Origin: https://app.arzansite.com" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --cookie-jar cookies.txt \
  --data '{"email":"user@example.com","password":"Password123!"}'

# 2) Use the session cookie to access receipts
curl -i https://nest.arzansite.com/api/receipts \
  -H "Origin: https://app.arzansite.com" \
  -H "Accept: application/json" \
  --cookie cookies.txt
```

### Backend requirements to make this work
- CORS (NestJS):
  - Allow the frontend origin and credentials
  - Example:
    - origin: `['https://app.arzansite.com', 'https://arzansite.com', 'http://localhost:5173']`
    - credentials: `true`
- Cookie settings when you authenticate (login/session endpoints):
  - HttpOnly cookie name: `appwrite_jwt` (or your session cookie)
  - Options:
    - `httpOnly: true`
    - `secure: true` (required on HTTPS; turn on in production)
    - `sameSite: 'none'` (for cross-site cookies)
    - `domain: '.arzansite.com'` (so subdomains can send it)
    - `path: '/'`
    - `maxAge: 3600000` (example)
- Guards/middleware:
  - Every protected endpoint (e.g., `/receipts`, `/invoices`, `/profiles/me`) should accept either:
    - Authorization header: `Bearer <accessToken>`
    - OR `appwrite_jwt` from cookies (read via `cookie-parser`)
- Auth/session endpoints the UI expects:
  - `POST /api/auth/login` (sets cookie; can also return tokens)
  - `POST /api/auth/session-auth` (accepts `{ sessionId?, jwt?, email? }`, sets cookie)
  - `GET /api/auth/status` (checks current session via cookie or bearer)
  - `POST /api/auth/refresh` (refreshes bearer tokens if you support bearer)
  - `GET /api/profiles/me`, `GET /api/invoices`, `GET /api/receipts` must validate cookie session.

### How to verify quickly
1. Log out and log back in (to ensure the new token-bridge writes both `backend_access_token` and `access_token`).
2. Visit `/debug` and press:
   - “Run All Tests” in BackendConnectionTest
   - “Test Authentication Flow” and, if needed, “Bootstrap Cookie Session” in AuthFlowTest
   - In DebugApiTest, try `/auth/status`, `/profiles/me`, `/invoices`, `/receipts`
3. If `/invoices` or `/receipts` are 401, fix cookie and CORS as above.

If you need me to adjust the frontend to always rely solely on cookie-session (and never bearer), I can force `apiClient` to skip Authorization headers entirely. Right now it supports both, which is robust once the cookie is being set/accepted correctly.

- New page: `/debug` now contains all auth/connectivity diagnostics
- Debug components removed from `Wizard` and `Index` to keep UI clean
- Token bridging implemented so `apiClient` and session-based auth stay in sync
- Password reset wired to public endpoints via `apiClient`
- package.json: added `start` and `update` scripts

For protected endpoints, send either the session cookie or a Bearer token. Public endpoints don’t need either.
Recommended (browser apps):
Use session-based auth. Create it via POST /api/auth/session with an Appwrite JWT. Then call APIs with credentials: 'include' so the HttpOnly cookie appwrite_jwt is sent automatically. No Authorization header needed.
Non-browser clients (mobile/server-to-server):
Send Authorization: Bearer <token>. The guard accepts:
Backend-issued JWT (if you use that flow), or
Appwrite JWT (short-lived), which the guard validates with Appwrite.
Which endpoints need auth?
Auth not required: health, signup, verify email, password reset, OAuth start/callback (and Swagger docs).
Auth required: orders, uploads, wallets, invoices, payments, profiles, most business endpoints.
Tip:
In production, ensure your requests include cookies (credentials: 'include') and your origin is allowed by CORS.

### Why you still get 401 “No token provided”
Your protected requests are being sent with credentials: 'include' (cookie) and, if present, an Authorization Bearer. The backend is not detecting either. Fix on the backend:

- CORS
  - origin: ['https://app.arzansite.com','https://arzansite.com','http://localhost:5173']
  - credentials: true
  - allowedHeaders: include 'Authorization'
- Cookie for browser sessions
  - On session creation: POST /api/auth/session with body { jwt: '<Appwrite JWT>' }, set cookie:
    - name: appwrite_jwt
    - httpOnly: true, secure: true (prod), sameSite: 'none', domain: '.arzansite.com', path: '/'
- Guard must accept either:
  - Cookie: read `req.cookies.appwrite_jwt`
  - OR Authorization header: `Bearer <token>` from `req.headers.authorization`
- Expose an auth check endpoint: GET /api/auth/me (reads cookie or bearer)

Browser example (what the app expects):
```javascript
await fetch('https://nest.arzansite.com/api/auth/session', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  credentials: 'include',
  body: JSON.stringify({ jwt })
});

await fetch('https://nest.arzansite.com/api/profiles/me', { credentials: 'include' });
```

Curl check (cookie-session):
```bash
# Create session cookie
curl -i -X POST https://nest.arzansite.com/api/auth/session \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --cookie-jar cookies.txt \
  --data '{"jwt":"<APPWRITE_JWT>"}'

# Call protected endpoint using cookie
curl -i https://nest.arzansite.com/api/invoices \
  --cookie cookies.txt
```

Notes:
- Your current “Bootstrap Cookie Session” call to `/auth/session-auth` returns 400. If your backend standard is POST `/auth/session` with `{ jwt }`, implement that and we’ll switch the debug button to use it.

  - GET `/payments/test-connection` (must return success:true once config is valid)

Why status is inconsistent across pages
- Your backend isn’t accepting one or both auth modes consistently. The browser sends cookies only if:
  - The cookie is set as HttpOnly, Secure (on HTTPS), SameSite=None, Domain=.arzansite.com, Path=/, and
  - CORS has origin whitelisted and credentials: true.
- Several endpoints return “No token provided”, meaning neither the cookie nor Authorization header was read by the guard for that route. Ensure all protected routes read either req.cookies.appwrite_jwt or Authorization bearer.

Why Session ID shows “Missing” elsewhere
- We don’t store Appwrite sessionId unless you explicitly bootstrap it. If you rely solely on HttpOnly cookie, that’s fine; `sessionId` can be null. The important part is backend seeing the cookie or Bearer.

Why last login isn’t recorded in Appwrite via NestJS
- The backend must update Appwrite user metadata or a dedicated field on successful login. In your login/session route handler, call Appwrite’s update endpoint (or write to your DB) to set lastLogin = now. If you only validate JWT and set cookie without writing the timestamp, it won’t be recorded.

Backend checklist
- CORS: origin ['https://app.arzansite.com','https://arzansite.com','http://localhost:5173'], credentials true, allow Authorization header.
- Cookie set on session creation with HttpOnly/None/Secure/Domain=.arzansite.com/Path=/.

### Backend-only integration guide for the frontend
@NestJS 
- Auth endpoints (use these only; do not use Appwrite SDK client-side)
  - POST `/api/auth/signup` with `{ email, password, metadata? }`
  - POST `/api/auth/verify-email` with `{ token, userId? }`
  - POST `/api/auth/login` with `{ email, password }` → returns `{ access_token, refresh_token, user, session }`
  - POST `/api/auth/refresh` with `{ refresh_token }` → returns new `access_token`
  - GET `/api/auth/me` with `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`
  - POST `/api/auth/logout` with `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`

- Auth flow (no direct Appwrite):
  1) Signup → backend sends verification email via SMTP
  2) Verify (link points to frontend; frontend calls `/api/auth/verify-email`)
  3) Login → store `access_token` (memory/localStorage) and `refresh_token` (securely)
  4) On app start/page change → call `/api/auth/me`; on 401 → call `/api/auth/refresh`; if still 401 → force login
  5) Use `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` for all backend requests

- Why did your prior session-auth fail
  - You were posting `session.$id` to `/api/auth/session-auth`. Appwrite requires the session secret, not the id, so it returned 401 (“Invalid or expired session”).
  - With backend-only, stop using `/api/auth/session-auth` and `/api/auth/session`. Use `/api/auth/login` and `/api/auth/refresh` only.

- Email sending (backend-only via SMTP; not Appwrite)
  - Configure `.env`: `SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_USER`, `SMTP_PASS`, `SMTP_FROM`, `SMTP_SENDER_NAME`, `SMTP_SECURITY` (ssl|starttls)
  - Test/admin: POST `/api/emails/test` or `/api/emails/template` (admin only)
  - Auth flows (signup, verification, reset) already use backend SMTP via `EmailService`. No Appwrite email usage on the frontend.

- Wallet (deposit/top-up) flow
  - Start deposit: POST `/api/wallets/me/deposit` with `{ amount, description? }` → use `res.data.paymentUrl` to redirect
  - Verify after return: POST `/api/wallets/me/deposit/verify` with `{ authority }`
  - Balances/tx: GET `/api/wallets/me`, `/api/wallets/me/balance`, `/api/wallets/me/transactions?limit=&offset=`
  - Idempotency is enforced; duplicate credits are prevented

- Orders and designs (payload shape)
  - Create order: POST `/api/orders` with:
    - Top-level: `title`, `description`, `price`, optional `comments`, `total_pages`, `total_sections`
    - Structured wizard data under `wizardData` (not in `description`)
    - Optional: `siteType`, `sessionId`
  - Save design: POST `/api/orders/:orderId/design` with `{ design: {...}, options?: {...} }`

- Profiles
  - GET `/api/profiles/me`
  - PATCH `/api/profiles/me` with only `{ full_name?, phone?, address? }`

- Payments (orders)
  - POST `/api/payments/request` with `{ orderId, amount, description, callbackUrl? }` → read `res.data.paymentUrl`, `res.data.authority`
  - POST `/api/payments/verify` with `{ orderId, authority, amount }` as needed

- CORS and headers
  - Use Authorization header, not cookies, for simplicity.
  - Ensure backend `CORS_ORIGINS` includes your frontend origin (e.g., `https://app.arzansite.com`).
  - No direct Appwrite calls; do not bundle Appwrite SDK in the frontend.

- Don’t do this on the frontend
  - No `account.createEmailPasswordSession`, no `account.createJWT`, no Appwrite client anywhere.
  - No calls to `https://app.arzansite.com/v1/*`. All calls go to `https://nest.arzansite.com/api/*`.

- Route prefix fixes you asked for
  - `wizard` and `domains` are now correctly available at:
    - `/api/wizard/*` (was /api/api/wizard/*)
    - `/api/domains/*` (was /api/api/domains/*)

- Minimal fetch examples
```ts
// login
const login = await fetch('/api/auth/login', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  body: JSON.stringify({ email, password })
}).then(r => r.json());
const { access_token, refresh_token } = login.data;

// auth me
const me = await fetch('/api/auth/me', {
  headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${access_token}` }
}).then(r => r.json());

// refresh
const refreshed = await fetch('/api/auth/refresh', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  body: JSON.stringify({ refresh_token })
}).then(r => r.json());

// wallet deposit
const dep = await fetch('/api/wallets/me/deposit', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: {
    'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    Authorization: `Bearer ${access_token}`
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({ amount: 3000000 })
}).then(r => r.json());
window.location.assign(dep.data.paymentUrl);
```

What changed
- Removed duplicate `api` prefixes from `wizard` and `domains` controllers so you won’t see `/api/api/...` anymore.
- Clarified and locked the frontend onto backend-only auth: use `/api/auth/login` + `/api/auth/refresh` instead of session-auth.
- Confirmed SMTP-based email service is in place and endpoints are available; frontend should never touch Appwrite for emails.

- I moved the auth/ping widgets to the dedicated debug page and fixed the debug tools to always send Authorization: Bearer when a token is present, plus credentials: 'include'. The duplicate React import on the debug page is fixed.

Why auth status looks inconsistent across pages
- You had a mix of cookie-session and bearer-token assumptions. Your backend-only integration expects Bearer for protected routes:
  - GET /api/auth/me requires Authorization: Bearer <access_token>
  - The cookie is not required and many routes will return “No token provided” if only the cookie is sent.
- I updated the debug testers to attach Bearer automatically (if found in storage). If you still see 401 on protected routes, your backend guard likely isn’t reading Authorization on those routes. Ensure your guard checks req.headers.authorization and accepts your backend-issued JWT.

Why “Session ID: ❌ Missing” shows on Debug
- With backend-only auth (no Appwrite SDK, no session cookie), there is no Appwrite session ID. That indicator can be ignored or hidden. If you want, I can remove the “Session ID” line from the debug UI.

Why last login isn’t recorded in Appwrite
- With backend-only auth, Appwrite isn’t involved in the login flow. Appwrite won’t update last login automatically. You must:
  - Update your NestJS login handler to write lastLogin (and lastActivity) either in your own DB/user profile, or call Appwrite Admin SDK to set a custom attribute. Without this explicit write, it stays unchanged.

What the frontend sends now
- Login: POST /api/auth/login → stores access_token + refresh_token.
- Protected requests: always send Authorization: Bearer <access_token>. Cookie is optional and ignored for auth.
- On 401: call POST /api/auth/refresh with { refresh_token } and retry.

Backend must allow this
- CORS: allow your frontend origin and the Authorization header. You don’t need credentials: true if you aren’t using cookies for auth.
- Guards on protected endpoints must accept Bearer and validate your backend-issued JWT.

If you want, I can:
- Remove the “Session ID” row in `AuthFlowTest` and delete the cookie-session helper from the debug page.
- Add a visible “Last login” column sourced from your backend profile response so you can confirm updates per login.
